title: Trace-context redaction orchestration and retention playbook for multi-tenant observability
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create an operational playbook and implementation plan to orchestrate redaction of PII from trace contexts and span payloads, define tenant-aware retention tiers, and add access/audit logging for every trace access path. This ticket covers ingestion-time sanitization, query-time masking, RBAC + audit trails for trace viewers, and the runtime controls needed to avoid large latency regressions on hot paths.

Background: Traces currently capture request metadata (headers, full prompt strings for debug) and raw span annotations. For multi-tenant customers and regulated workspaces, retaining raw prompts in traces is a compliance risk. We need a deterministic, token-aware redaction strategy that is reversible for internal debugging with strict audit controls, plus retention automation that can be configured per-tenant/route.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Schema updates: formalize which trace/span fields are "sensitive_candidates" (http.headers, request.prompt, sql.query, user_id, session_cookie) and which are metadata-only.
2) Ingestion pipeline: implement a redaction adapter in the trace collector that applies pattern-based and tokenizer-aware scrubbing. Support two redaction modes: irreversible scrub (default for hosted) and reversible pseudonymization (for Dedicated/Private with KMS).
3) Retention orchestration: implement retention policy service to apply tiered expirations (default 30d for full spans, 90d for reduced spans, 365d metadata-only). Allow per-tenant overrides via tenant profile with policy inheritance.
4) RBAC + access logging: require explicit trace_access permission for raw traces; every access logs an immutable audit event with user, role, org, reason, and query fingerprint. Build dashboard for audit review.
5) Query-time masking: add on-demand masking layer for ad-hoc queries to prevent accidental leaks when users download or export spans.
6) Tests and validation: unit tests for scrubbing rules, integration tests with sample traces, property tests to ensure no leakage of blacklisted patterns, and load-tests to measure latency impact.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Tokenizer-aware redaction reduces false positives but requires model-tokenizer alignment; dependency on tokenizer library upgrade (see dependencies).
- Reversible pseudonymization implies key management and additional operational burden; constrained to Dedicated/Private customers.
- Ingestion-time redaction trades off early protection for increased CPU work on collectors; we will introduce a sampling throttle for low-priority telemetry to preserve latency SLOs.

Operational runbook snippets and links:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.company/obs/trace-redaction-playbook (draft)
- Design doc PR: https://github.com/redwood/observability/pull/1289
- Related incident learnings: https://internal.redwood.company/incidents/2025-12-trace-leakage

Acceptance criteria:
- Redaction adapter merged and enabled behind feature flag "trace_redaction_v2".
- Retention policy service can configure per-tenant expiry and report counts in retention dashboard.
- Audit log emits on every raw-trace access and is queryable from the Console with appropriate RBAC.
- End-to-end tests demonstrate zero retention of raw prompts after configured window in irreversible mode.
- Performance impact on p50 trace ingestion latency <= +10% in our baseline load tests.
acceptance_criteria: feature flag trace_redaction_v2 gated and documented
per-tenant retention policy configurable via Console and API
audit events emitted for raw-trace read with user/role/reason
integration tests show no raw prompt retention after irreversible window
p50 ingest latency regression <= 10% under baseline load

testing_plan: Unit tests for regex/tokenizer rules (CI coverage)
Integration tests that ingest sample traces with PII patterns and assert post-ingest redact/no-retain behavior
